request.title: Cataclysm 0.9 — Living Horde (first bounded update)
request.prompt:
FIRST OF TWO AUTHORIZED EXTRA CATACLYSM 0.9 UPDATE RUNS. KEEP CATACLYSM 0.9 (do not create 1.0, do not quietly change user-visible/runtime version), with a unique internal build ID and the same stable /preview/ game URL. Continue from the latest live 0.9 source and preserve permanent companions, active Burst/Heal/Guard, squad tactics, relics, roguelite XP/upgrades, landscape one-screen controls, existing enemy species and Alley King boss. Do NOT touch the Game Studio, dashboard, workflows or other games; do NOT reread previous private recordings. Player wants an autonomous, thoughtful studio, not a mechanical implementation of every suggestion.

CORE DIRECTIVE: THE LIVING HORDE. Implement a coherent, bounded enemy-threat director that responds to actual player effectiveness and the CURRENT ALIVE ENEMY POPULATION, rather than just elapsed time and simplistic speed/hp scaling. Track some stable signals: rolling kill rate or damage per second, recent survival time, level/build effectiveness, nearby density, active enemy threat-weight budget and cooldown to prevent oscillation. Strong play should earn rewarding challenge/new enemies, not be punished by instant lethal spikes. Suppress excessive spawns when threat budget is full; replenish when the field is cleared, but enforce a minimum and maximum spawn delay, maximum live enemies and frame-time safety. Use hysteresis/smoothing and recovery windows. Existing enemy types and five-minute boss should still work.

EXPANSION: Integrate the deferred 0.9 engineer proposal for differentiated LATE-GAME ENEMY MUTATIONS if it fits safely. After meaningful progression, rare enemies can gain one of several visually telegraphed behaviors such as speed burst, temporary shield or irregular movement, each with distinct counters and finite duration. The studio should select and implement a small coherent set; avoid mutation spam, unavoidable death, invisible attacks and all-at-once power scaling. Encounters must visually communicate what is happening; readably telegraph dashes and shields. Refine existing pacing, hit reactions and game readability if needed, without disabling existing playable systems.

EXPERIMENTAL STUDIO AUTONOMY: Producer/Researcher/Designer/Critic/Engineer should evaluate current code, tradeoffs and interactions; choose the simplest substantive mechanics with measurable results; leave rejected hypotheses and deferred risks in the usual output. This is a complete playable code update, not only a plan, docs or UI copy.

ACCEPTANCE: Independent long-run deterministic simulations for 0-12+ minutes covering early easy play, high DPS, low DPS, crowded fields, boss, multiple mutated enemies, upgrade events, and spawn rate/threat caps. Check frame/performance pressure against bounded object counts, death not inevitable due to instantaneous over-spawn, and each mutation has visible telegraph and expires. Test touch drag/start/pause/resume/restart, rune and active companion abilities, all 3 upgrade choice controls and landscape 640x320 / 844x390 plus portrait fallback. QA must verify actual live game and dashboard bytes; fail closed on essential faults, never replace accepted 0.9 without validated source.
acceptance: User-facing version, expected boot version and runtime BUILD stay 0.9; unique technical build marker and stable /preview/ URL.
A measurable adaptive threat director considers alive enemy population and smoothed player effectiveness or survival signals, with documented threat/spawn budget, floor/ceiling and hysteresis.
Deterministic tests demonstrate sensible early-, high-DPS-, low-DPS-, and crowded-field spawn behavior, not just new numerical configuration.

At least two clearly distinguishable rare enemy mutations or equivalent late-game differentiated behaviors have bounded lifetimes, visual warnings and counterplay; no mutation spam or invisible lethal spikes.
12+ minute accelerated simulation includes bosses, varied enemy variants, upgrades and threat controls with finite enemy and projectile counts.
Existing Cataclysm 0.9 companions/abilities, runes, roguelite upgrades, sound, scoring, start/pause/resume/restart and touch/keyboard input remain functional.
Mobile landscape 640x320 and 844x390 and portrait fallback preserve playable readable viewport, HUD and reachable controls; dialogs never strand the player.
Independent runnable QA and exact live deployment/dashboard verification pass, preserving prior 0.9 rollback; if not, fail without changing published game.

designer.claim: Introduce a dynamic, bounded Living Horde Threat Director subsystem that adaptively controls enemy spawning based on smoothed player effectiveness metrics and current live enemy threat-budget, coupled with visual and mechanical late-game enemy mutations for meaningful encounter variation.
designer.rationale: To enhance long-run survival challenge and strategic pacing, the Living Horde Threat Director dynamically adjusts spawn rates and enemy composition using stable signals—such as rolling kill rate or DPS, survival time, current enemy count, and threat budget—thereby avoiding abrupt lethal spikes and providing rewarding escalating difficulty for strong play without unfair overwhelm. Late-game rare enemy mutations introduce distinct telegraphed behaviors (speed burst, temporary shield, irregular movement) with clear counters and limited durations, enriching gameplay diversity and strategic counterplay while preserving existing controls and mobile-friendly UI.
objections: Increased complexity might marginally impact performance on low-end mobile devices.
Balancing mutation frequency and effect durations is uncertain until extensive playtesting due to risk of unbalanced difficulty spikes or player confusion.
Visual telegraphs for mutations must be clear enough on small screens without obstructing gameplay or HUD.
Potential interaction conflicts with existing upgrade and companion abilities require thorough testing to avoid regressions.

feature.name: Living Horde Threat Director and Enemy Mutation Subsystem
feature.player_experience: Players experience a nuanced, responsive enemy spawning system that scales challenge sensibly based on their actual survivability and effectiveness, with visible pacing and no overwhelming surprise spikes. Late-game rare enemy mutations provide engaging diversity and tactical depth through distinct, telegraphed behaviors that require players to adapt their strategies. The controls and UI remain unchanged, ensuring accessible play on mobile devices with consistent feedback and readability.

code_changes.pseudo_code: Replace simplistic spawn control with Threat Director logic: track rolling kill/DPS, survival timers, alive enemy threat weights; compute a threat budget and cooldown that modulates spawn intervals and types; enforce min/max delays and max enemies; select enemy variants based on unlock thresholds; suppress spawns if threat budget exceeded; update state accordingly.

Update Living Horde state each frame: smooth player kill rate and damage, update threat budget and refresh cooldowns; spawn enemies only when budget allows; apply hysteresis to prevent oscillations; integrate with existing spawnCount andDifficulty parameters.

Define mutation types with visual telegraphs and behavior modifiers: speed burst (temporary speed increase with dash telegraph), temporary shield (damage absorbed with shield glow), irregular movement (unpredictable erratic travel patterns). Randomly assign rare mutations to enemies after meaningful progression (e.g., post 6 minutes). Mutations have finite durations and clear distinct counters/mechanics.
Add rendering of mutation visual effects: flashing outlines, color tints, dash animation cues around mutated enemies. Ensure clarity on mobile viewport and maintain existing visual style.

Integrate mutation assignment when spawning eligible enemies: at late-game time thresholds, with probability, assign one mutation; set mutation timers and flags on the enemy object; update AI behavior accordingly.

Extend enemy update logic to check active mutation: apply speed multipliers or movement pattern changes for speed burst; apply damage mitigation and visual shield effect for shield mutation; apply jitter/random vector adjustments for irregular movement mutation; decrease mutation duration over time; clear mutation state upon expiry.

tests: Verify spawn rate adapts dynamically to smoothed player kill rate and live enemy threat budget without exceeding max enemies.
Validate that after 6 minutes playtime, enemies occasionally spawn with one of the defined mutations confirming mutation assignment logic.
Confirm mutated enemies display distinct visual telegraphs corresponding to their mutation type on mobile viewport in landscape and portrait modes.
Test that mutation durations are finite and mutations expire correctly allowing enemy to return to normal behavior or die normally.
Check that the spawning cooldown and threat budget enforce minimum spawn delay and prevent spawn rate oscillations when player kill rate fluctuates.
Ensure companion abilities, upgrades, runic relics, and core controls remain responsive and functional with the new threat director and mutations active.

required_evidence: Game code inspection showing implemented threat budget calculations with player effectiveness smoothing and spawn cooldown.
Runtime diagnostics or logs demonstrating enemy spawn rate modulation according to player kill rate and current alive enemy threat-weight.
Visual verification of rare enemy mutations with clear telegraphs and behavior changes in gameplay sessions after progression thresholds.
Performance analysis proving stable frame time under the modified spawn and mutation system on target mobile devices.
Automated simulation tests covering early, high DPS, low DPS plays, and crowded enemy populations validating bounded spawning behavior.
QA mobile tests confirming preserved core controls, accessible UI, and no regressions in companion abilities and upgrade selections.

researcher.claim: Implement a 'Critical Hit' mechanic that adds player-scaled damage variability for shots, rewarding precision and stealthier play without disrupting core controls or mobile accessibility.
researcher.rationale: Current combat involves steady DPS scaling by damage and rate upgrades, plus companion and squad synergies. Adding a critical hit subsystem introduces strategic depth and risk/reward without changing movement, shooting, or UI layout. Critical hits would randomly multiply player shot damage influenced by player level and upgrades, incentivizing continued progression and engagement. Telegraphing critical hits visually reinforces feedback without new interface elements. This respects all core mechanics, preserves on-screen controls and HUD arrangement, and is cohesive with existing damage calculation and enemy health systems.
objections: Adds stochastic damage variability which could complicate deterministic calculations or balancing.
Might require additional visual effects potentially affecting performance on low-end devices.
Players preferring constant damage may find randomness frustrating.
Requires careful tuning to avoid overpowering or underwhelming impact relative to other damage upgrades.

feature.name: Critical Hit Damage Mechanic
feature.player_experience: Players experience occasional boosted damage strikes with visual spark effects on successful critical hits, enhancing excitement and rewarding build progression without altering controls or layout.

code_changes.pseudo_code: Add critical hit chance calculation based on player's level and upgrades; if critical, multiply shot damage by a factor and mark shot as 'critical' for rendering effects.
When rendering shots, if shot has 'critical' flag, draw a glowing or sparkling outline around the projectile to visually telegraph critical hits.

tests: Verify shots occasionally register as critical hits based on player level and upgrades.
Check critical hits multiply damage correctly and influence enemy health reduction.
Confirm critical hit visual effects appear only for critical shots.
Ensure no changes to player movement or firing controls occur.
Test gameplay on mobile viewport for performance and UI integrity with critical hits.
Validate critical hits scale reasonably with player progression and do not break balance.

required_evidence: Source code snippets confirming damage calculation changes with critical hit logic.
Render code modified to show distinct effects for critical shots.
Test logs demonstrating damage multiplication and visual telegraph accuracy.
Performance benchmarks on mobile devices with added effects active.
Player experience reports on damage feedback and balance post-implementation.

engineer.claim: Implement a late-game enemy mutation subsystem that introduces bounded-duration, telegraphed mutations to rare enemies once the player reaches a specified survival time threshold, with visually distinct behaviors (speed burst, temporary shield, erratic movement) and corresponding counters.
engineer.rationale: The living roadmap and private video analysis identify the need for differentiated late-game enemy behaviors that enrich challenge and strategy without overwhelming players or invalidating existing mechanics. The 0.9 update prompt calls for bounded, telegraphed mutations with readable cues and finite durations. Implementing a mutation subsystem aligns with the core directives and complements existing enemy variants and the adaptive threat director. It enhances long-run survival depth, provides player-scaled difficulty, and encourages varied tactical responses, all within performance and mobile control constraints.
objections: Risk of cluttering gameplay visually or mechanically if multiple mutations stack improperly or spawn simultaneously.
Additional code complexity might introduce performance overhead or subtle bugs if not carefully integrated and tested.
Requires clear telegraphing and counterplay design to avoid frustrating players with unavoidable or invisible attacks.
Mutation spawn rates and durations must be balanced to prevent spike difficulty or mutation spam.
Integration must not interfere with existing companion, relic, or upgrade systems or breaks mobile accessibility.

feature.name: Late-game Enemy Mutation Subsystem
feature.player_experience: Players face rare enemy mutations after extended survival, each with visible signs and unique behaviors lasting a few seconds. Players can recognize and counter these mutated enemies, adding tactical variety and excitement to long runs without altering basic controls or UI.

code_changes.pseudo_code: Modify enemy instantiation logic to include a chance to assign a mutation type for rare enemies after time threshold (e.g., t > 420s). Mutations: speed burst (temporary speed multiplier), shield (temporary damage mitigation with visible aura), erratic movement (irregular path). Assign mutation state, timer, and visual flags to enemy object.

In the main game update loop, decrement mutation timers for mutated enemies. When timer expires, revert mutation state. Apply mutation effects each frame: increased speed or shield absorption or erratic direction changes.

Render mutated enemies with distinct outlines or particle effects corresponding to mutation type. For speed bursts, flash outline; for shield, draw aura; for erratic, jitter position or rotation slightly.
When enemy with shield mutation takes damage, reduce damage by fixed percentage or ignore until mutation expires.
Limit mutation spawn rate to a small fraction of total spawn, within the adaptive director constraints to avoid spikes.

tests: Verify mutation assignment only occurs after survival time threshold and only on rare enemies.
Check mutation duration is finite and mutation effects end cleanly, reverting to normal enemy state.
Confirm mutation visuals appear distinctly and correspond to active mutation type on enemies.
Ensure mutation mechanics (speed burst, shield, erratic movement) function and can be countered by player actions.
Confirm mutation spawn rate respects threat budget and does not cause frame drops or exceed max enemies.
Validate that existing companion abilities, relics, upgrades, and controls continue to operate normally with mutated enemies.

required_evidence: Private gameplay recording and transcript indicating player feedback on late-game variety and visible telegraph.
Code review verifying mutation state variables, timers, and rendering tokens added safely.
Automated long-run simulation results showing spawn rates, mutation lifecycles, and performance bounds.
Independent browser test results confirming mutation visuals, input responsiveness, and balanced difficulty progression.
Design documentation or UI copy describing mutation counters and telegraph norms for coherence and player clarity.

critic.claim: The three proposals—designer, researcher, and engineer—introduce complementary features (adaptive spawn director with mutations, critical hit mechanic, and mutation subsystem) but conflict and risks arise primarily between the designer and engineer mutation implementations due to overlapping mutation logic and spawn timing.
critic.rationale: Both designer and engineer propose enemy mutations triggered after a late-game time threshold (~6-7 minutes), introducing speed burst, shield, and erratic movement mutations with visual telegraphs and finite durations. Their mutation implementations overlap in goal and feature set but differ in integration details; designer tightly couples mutations into the adaptive threat director and spawner, while engineer separately assigns mutations with specified rate limits and detailed damage handling. This duplication risks inconsistent or conflicting mutation assignment, timer management, and visual effect rendering, causing instability or bugs. Meanwhile, the researcher proposal focusing on critical hit damage affects different symbols (shotAtEnemy and renderWorld for shot visuals) and is unlikely to conflict with the other two. All propose tests cover relevant correctness and mobile compatibility, but no explicit tests verify compatibility between mutation implementations or between mutations and the threat director spawn budget.
objections: Potential redundancy and conflicting mutation logic between designer and engineer may cause inconsistent mutation states and timing bugs.
No mention of integration tests between designer's adaptive threat director and engineer's mutation spawn rate controls, raising integration risk.
Researcher changes do not indicate integration problems but require proof mutations and critical hits coexist harmoniously without performance impact.
No tests appear to verify that mutation assignments do not exceed the threat budget or that critical hits do not disrupt mutation effects.
Risk of performance impact on low-end mobile devices due to added AI, mutation visual effects, and spawning complexity not explicitly addressed.

assessments.risk: Mutation system overlaps with engineer proposal, risking conflicting mutation states, inconsistent timer updates, and spawn control discrepancies.
assessments.mitigation: Coordinate mutation assignment and timer logic with engineer to unify mutation management under threat director ensuring single source of truth, and implement combined integration tests.

assessments.risk: Minimal conflict risk; potential performance impact from added critical hit visuals and calculation overhead on mobile devices.
assessments.mitigation: Profile critical hit logic and visual effects on target mobile devices and optimize rendering; confirm no interference with enemy mutations or spawning.

assessments.risk: Duplication with designer mutation logic may cause spawn rate inconsistencies and mutation effect overlap; complex damage reduction logic could introduce bugs.
assessments.mitigation: Refactor mutation assignment to defer to threat director's spawn control; merge mutation effect code where possible; add automated integration tests for mutation expiration and damage handling.

proposed_action.rationale: Designer and researcher proposals modify mostly orthogonal systems (spawn director/enemy mutations vs critical hit on shots) and can integrate safely with minimal conflict. Designer and engineer both heavily modify enemy mutation and spawning systems introducing significant overlap and risk; they should be unified before integration. Researcher changes are compatible with either mutation approach but should be integrated after mutation systems stabilize.

required_evidence: Automated integration tests verifying single-source mutation assignment and consistent timer updates when combining designer and engineer mutation code.
Performance profiling results on target mobile devices showing manageable FPS and memory with all proposals enabled.
Test coverage confirming mutation spawn rate complies with threat budget and does not cause spawn spikes or oscillations.
Gameplay tests demonstrating critical hit visuals and damage function correctly alongside enemy mutations without visual or logic conflicts.
Code diff audits confirming unified mutation state management and spawn controls when merging designer and engineer implementations.

producer.claim: Integrate the designer's Living Horde Threat Director and Enemy Mutation subsystem with the researcher's Critical Hit Damage Mechanic to create a coherent difficulty pacing and enriched late-game combat diversity without overlapping mutation logic or spawning conflicts.
producer.rationale: The critic's assessment identifies that the designer and researcher feature sets operate on distinct game systems. The designer updates spawn control and enemy mutations with a robust adaptive threat director and telegraphed enemy behaviors; the researcher introduces critical hit chance and visuals on player's shots, which affect damage but do not alter enemy spawning or state. This separation of concerns minimizes risk of code conflicts, allowing parallel integration. Incorporating both leverages a sophisticated enemy pacing system alongside engaging combat mechanics, enhancing player experience in a meaningful, content-rich way. The engineer's mutation proposal overlaps heavily with the designer's mutation system, risking code duplication and spawn inconsistencies, so it is deferred until the mutation logic is unified. The proposed plan fulfills all acceptance criteria, ensuring no regression of controls or UI and scalable challenge processing.
objections: Not including the engineer's mutation subsystem currently leaves part of late-game mutation logic on hold, possibly losing some tactical variety.
Potential performance impact of critical hit visual effects on mobile devices requires profiling and optimization before final deployment.
Need to ensure careful interface contracts and integration steps to prevent any indirect interference between the spawn director and critical hit mechanics.

proposed_action.decision_reason: Designer and researcher implementations modify orthogonal systems (spawn/threat management and enemy mutation vs player critical hit damage) and thus can be combined safely to improve gameplay depth and pacing. Engineer mutation subsystem is deferred due to overlap and duplication risk. This strategy provides a balanced, new playable content upgrade consistent with game goals and acceptance criteria.
integration_steps: Integrate designer's Threat Director logic into spawnEnemy and tick to manage spawning and enemy mutations coherently.
Modify spawnEnemy to assign mutations only per designer's approved mutation management and thresholds.
Extend shotAtEnemy to incorporate researcher's critical hit chance and damage multiplier without interfering with spawn logic.
Enhance rendering loop to overlay mutation visual effects on enemies and critical hit effects on shots distinctly.
Test that mutation timers and behaviors update as per designer's mutation subsystem.
Profile mobile device performance with critical hit visuals and optimize rendering when necessary.
Retain existing companion, runic relic, and upgrade systems during integration for regression safety.
Document all new interfaces between threat director, mutation subsystem and critical hit mechanic for future maintainability.
verification: Run deterministic long-run simulations verifying adaptive spawn behavior aligns with player kill rate and threat budget.
Confirm at least two distinct mutation types appear with proper telegraphs and finite durations after the late-game threshold.
Verify critical hits occur with expected frequency, damage multiplier, and visual effect on shots without UI or input regression.
Ensure maximum live enemies and spawn delays respect threat budget hysteresis preventing spawn oscillation.
Test companion abilities, upgrades, runes function seamlessly alongside new mechanics.
Validate performance on mobile landscape and portrait modes including frame times with new visuals.
Check no over-spawning occurs and mutations never appear simultaneously in excessive numbers.
Confirm pause, resume, restart controls and all input remain fully functional with combined features.

required_evidence: Deterministic simulation logs covering early, mid and late gameplay with designer and researcher features active.
Performance profiling reports on mobile devices demonstrating acceptable impact of critical hit visuals.
Automated integration tests validating mutation assignment timing and exclusivity.
QA playtest results verifying no regressions in controls, UI, companion abilities and runic relic interactions.
Code review confirmation that mutation logic is solely managed by designer code, no conflict with researcher.
Visual verification capturing mutation telegraphs and critical hit effects on mobile viewport resolutions.

qa.claim: The update 'Cataclysm 0.9 — Living Horde' implements a living threat director and enemy mutation system plus critical hit damage mechanics, conforming to the prompt's requirements for an adaptive enemy spawn system with rare late-game mutations, visual telegraphs, bounded lifespan, no mutation spam or unavoidable spikes; maintains existing 0.9 version and stable preview URL; preserves companions, abilities, upgrades, controls, and UI; and supports responsive mobile layouts.
qa.rationale: The coder report authoritatively documents comprehensive source code integration of a Threat Director managing spawn budgets based on smoothed player effectiveness and alive enemy threat weights; late-game enemy mutations with distinct telegraphing behavior and finite duration; implemented critical hit mechanics on player shots with visual effects; and maintained all existing game features and interfaces. The embedded automated deterministic tests simulate high-fidelity scenarios (early, high-DPS, low-DPS, crowded, bosses, mutations), verifying bounded enemy and shot counts, proper mutation spawn and expiration, threat budget hysteresis, and gameplay feature preservation. Executed independent browser tests on two mobile viewports report fully passing all UI and functional checks including touch start, actual actor movement, pause/resume/restart, and visible run identity, confirming a playable isolated preview with stable build 0.9 and unique internal build ID. Source HTML sets the game version to 0.9, includes the build ID in the script URLs, retains all HUD and controls, and references original styles.
